input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The guard uses all(...) instead of any(...) over the arguments' help attributes, so the section is gated on every argument being documented rather than on at least one.
- failure path: A command with arguments SRC (help set) and DST (no help) prints no 'Positional arguments' section at all in --help, silently dropping the documented text; conversely a command with zero arguments satisfies all([]) and prints an empty 'Positional arguments' header on every --help.

Reviewer finding
- description: For a command with no Argument parameters, all() over an empty list returns True, so the 'Positional arguments' section heading is written even though there is nothing to list. The original `if args:` guard is gone.
- rationale: Trigger: any command that defines only options (no arguments), which is very common. args is [], all(...) is True, so formatter.section(...) runs and writes the heading. HelpFormatter.section writes the heading unconditionally, and write_dl with no rows adds nothing. Impact: every such command's --help output gains an empty 'Positional arguments:' heading, a visible regression on a common path.
critique: The finding points to the same faulty all() guard. It describes the label's own secondary failure: all([]) is True, so an empty 'Positional arguments' header gets printed. It leaves out the mixed help case, but the operation and the way it goes wrong are the same.
